method_card.title: Sport and Staying Active
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sport vocabulary, the difference between jugar a and hacer, frequency expressions, and using the preterite and imperfect to talk about sport habits past and present.

SpanishEnglish
el fútbolfootball
el baloncestobasketball
el tenistennis
la nataciónswimming
el ciclismocycling
correrto run
ir al gimnasioto go to the gym
mantenerse en formato keep fit
es bueno para la saludit is good for health
dos veces a la semanatwice a week
todos los díasevery day
los fines de semanaat weekends
el atletismoathletics
la equitaciónhorse riding
reduce el estrés (Higher)it reduces stress

Grammar focus — jugar a vs hacer: Use jugar a for ball/team sports: juego al fútbol, juega al tenis. Note the contraction a + el = al. Use hacer for individual activities: hago natación, hace atletismo. Jugar is stem-changing (u→ue) in the present tense: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan. Hacer is irregular in yo only: hago.

Grammar focus — imperfect vs preterite: Use the imperfect for habitual past actions: Cuando era joven, jugaba al rugby todos los fines de semana (When I was young, I used to play rugby every weekend). Use the preterite for a specific completed event: Ayer jugué al tenis con mi hermano (Yesterday I played tennis with my brother).

Model: Juego al fútbol dos veces a la semana porque es divertido y me mantiene en forma. Cuando era pequeño, hacía natación. Ayer corrí cinco kilómetros en el parque. (I play football twice a week because it is fun and keeps me fit. When I was young, I used to go swimming. Yesterday I ran five kilometres in the park.)
steps: Learn sport vocabulary with the correct verb — jugar a for ball sports, hacer for individual activities
Master the stem-change in jugar (u→ue): juego, juegas, juega
Use frequency expressions: dos veces a la semana, todos los días, los fines de semana
Practice the imperfect (habitual past) vs preterite (single completed event) for sport

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — sport and healthy living appear across all papers every year

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Hago natación tres veces a la semana porque me mantiene en forma.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hago natación = I do swimming. Use hacer (not jugar) for swimming — it is an individual activity.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: tres veces a la semana = three times a week. porque me mantiene en forma = because it keeps me fit.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I go swimming three times a week because it keeps me fit.

worked_examples.question: Which verb do you use: 'Yo _____ al baloncesto' — jugar or hacer?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Basketball is a team/ball sport, so use jugar a.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Jugar is stem-changing (u→ue) in the yo form: juego. With al (a + el): juego al baloncesto.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Juego al baloncesto — use jugar a for team/ball sports.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish sports to their English meaning
Match the Spanish phrases to their English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: al fútbol todos los sábados y mi hermana

gaps.correct_explain: juego is the yo form of jugar. The stem u changes to ue. Use jugar a for ball/team sports.

wrong.hago: hago means 'I do/make'. For ball sports like football, use jugar a, not hacer.
wrong.juega: juega is the él/ella form. The subject is 'yo' → juego.

gaps.correct_explain: hace is the ella form of hacer. Use hacer for individual activities like swimming.

wrong.juega: juega means 'she plays' (ball sport). Swimming is not a ball sport → use hace natación.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: El deporte es bueno para la

gaps.correct_explain: salud means health. Es bueno para la salud = It is good for health.

wrong.forma: forma means form/shape. The correct phrase is es bueno para la salud.

gaps.correct_explain: energía means energy. Me da energía = It gives me energy.

wrong.estrés: estrés means stress — the sentence is about the positive benefits of sport → energía.

bronze.question: What does 'Juego al baloncesto dos veces a la semana' mean?
options: I play basketball twice a week
I watch basketball twice a week
I will play basketball this week

bronze.source_text: Me encanta hacer ejercicio porque es bueno para la salud y me mantiene en forma.
model_answers: I love exercising because it is good for your health and it keeps me fit.
hints: mantenerse en forma = to keep fit

silver.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: al tenis con mi hermano y
silver.english: Yesterday I played tennis with my brother and we ran in the park.

gaps.correct_explain: jugué is the yo preterite form of jugar. Note the spelling change: g → gu before e to preserve the /g/ sound.

wrong.juego: juego is the present tense. Ayer (yesterday) requires the preterite: jugué.
wrong.jugó: jugó is the él/ella preterite form. Subject is 'I' → jugué.

gaps.correct_explain: corrimos is the nosotros preterite of correr. Regular -er preterite ending: -imos.

wrong.corremos: corremos is the present tense. Ayer requires the preterite: corrimos.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Mi hermano juega la natación todos los días.
silver.explanation: Swimming is an individual activity, not a ball sport. Use hacer (hace natación), not jugar. Jugar a is for team/ball sports like football or tennis.
silver.translation: My brother does swimming every day.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: I do athletics after school because it gives me energy.

distractor_labels.Juego: wrong verb — athletics is an individual sport, so use hacer (Hago), not jugar

silver.source_text: I go to the gym three times a week because it keeps me fit.
model_answers: Voy al gimnasio tres veces a la semana porque me mantiene en forma.
hints: three times a week = tres veces a la semana
to keep fit = mantenerse en forma

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: I do sport not only because it is fun, but also because it reduces stress.

distractor_labels.Juego: wrong verb — deporte (sport in general) uses hacer, not jugar
distractor_labels.pero: wrong connective — 'not only... but also' = no solo... sino también, not pero
distractor_labels.aburrido: wrong meaning — the English says 'fun' (divertido), not 'boring' (aburrido)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre in Spain and the receptionist asks about your sport and fitness habits.

bullets.prompt: Say what sport you play and how often.
bullets.model_answer: Juego al fútbol dos veces a la semana con mi equipo del instituto.
bullets.note: juego al fútbol (definite article after jugar a) + frequency phrase

bullets.prompt: Explain why exercise is important to you.
bullets.model_answer: El ejercicio es importante porque me mantiene en forma y reduce el estrés.

bullets.prompt: Say what sport you did when you were younger.
bullets.model_answer: Cuando era pequeño, hacía natación los fines de semana.
bullets.note: cuando era (imperfect of ser) + hacía (imperfect of hacer) for habitual past

bullets.prompt: Say what sport you would like to try in the future and why.
bullets.model_answer: En el futuro me gustaría probar el esquí porque sería emocionante.
bullets.note: me gustaría + infinitive (conditional = polite); sería (conditional of ser)

gold.question: Complete the sentence
gold.english: If I had more time, I would do more exercise every day.

gaps.correct_explain: tuviera is the imperfect subjunctive of tener. After si in a hypothetical condition ('if I had'), use the imperfect subjunctive.

wrong.tengo: tengo is the present indicative. Hypothetical 'if' clauses use the imperfect subjunctive → tuviera.
wrong.tenía: tenía is the imperfect indicative. The hypothetical si clause needs the imperfect subjunctive → tuviera.

gaps.correct_explain: haría is the yo conditional of hacer. The main clause of a hypothetical 'if' sentence uses the conditional.

wrong.hago: hago is the present tense. The main clause of a hypothetical 'if' sentence needs the conditional → haría.
